Hi Karthik —

We're finalizing our vendor security review for the Q4 rollout and have a couple of outstanding items related to model training and log retention. Two specific asks from procurement/security: 

1) Explicit statement that Acme customer content will not be used to train or improve Redwood public models ("no-training" assurance) unless we expressly opt in in writing.
2) Clarify retention windows for request/response logs and a process for verified deletion. Acme's standard is 90 days for application logs; is that negotiable? We also need a sample clause to add to the SOW/DPA and an estimate for how long deletion requests take to complete.

Can you confirm and share any supporting docs (SOC2 summary, deletion workflow)? If you already have standard contract language for the "no-training" assurance, that would speed things up.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Samantha Lee
Director, Cloud Integrations
Acme, Inc.

Hi Samantha —

Short answer: yes, we can provide a firm "no-training" assurance for your account and a documented deletion process. High-level points to save time:

- Hosted API: By default we do not use customer prompt/response content to train our public models for general improvement. We do have an opt-in mechanism for customers that want training benefits.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: Customer data is never used for model training or shared outside the tenant (this is standard).
- Retention: Default request/response logs for hosted API are retained 30 days. We can negotiate a longer window (90 days) for enterprise customers with a contractual commitment.
- Deletion requests: We provide a verified deletion workflow. For hosted customers, deletion of request/response logs is typically completed within 48–72 hours after validation; for Dedicated/Private, deletion is under customer control and can be completed on-prem as defined in the SOW.

I'm attaching our SOC 2 summary and a high-level data-deletion procedure. Looping in Neha from our security team for the formal contract language. If that sounds right, I can shoot over a DPA addendum with the explicit "no-training" clause and (separately) options for a 90-day retention window.

Next steps:
- Neha will propose exact clause language for the DPA.
- I can send the DocuSign for the DPA + retention amendment once agreed.

Thanks,
Karthik

Hi Samantha / Karthik —

Thanks for the note. I pulled together the language and some operational detail below that you can use in the DPA. I kept it succinct so your legal team can slot it directly into the contract; happy to expand where needed.

Proposed DPA excerpt (plain language):
"Redwood Inference represents and warrants that it will not use Customer Content to train, improve, or otherwise modify Redwood public model weights or shared model artifacts, unless Customer provides prior written consent that explicitly describes the scope of such training. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood will not use Customer Content for training under any circumstances."

Operational notes: 
- Training assurances: We maintain a formal internal control (a technical and policy flag) that prevents ingestion of customer content into training pipelines unless a documented opt-in is recorded and approved by Product & Legal. We can provide attestation to this control for the purposes of your audit.
- Retention: Our standard retention for request/response logs (hosted) is 30 days. We can contractually extend retention to 90 days for enterprise customers for an additional fee and with an updated SLA. Extended retention is configurable per-customer and scoped in the SOW.
- Deletion process:
  - Verification: Customer must submit deletion request via our portal or signed email from an authorized admin.
  - Execution: For hosted accounts, engineering workflows purge logs and any derived indices; propagation to backups is scheduled and completed within 30 days. Primary deletion of active logs is usually completed within 48–72 hours.
  - Audit: We issue a signed deletion confirmation (PDF) with timestamps and job IDs; audit logs demonstrating the deletion operation are retained for one year for compliance purposes.

Edge cases / notes:
- Cache and telemetry: Application-level caches (e.g., prefix/KV caches) are tenant-scoped; we purge those as part of deletion workflows but advise customers to rotate keys if they are concerned about ephemeral in-memory state.
- Backups: Cold backups are on a 30–day rotation. We will schedule and document the removal of customer data from backups inside the 30-day window for hosted customers.

I'll attach a short attestation we can sign and include in the DPA if needed. Please let me know if Acme's security/legal wants different wording (for example, a commitment to complete backup purges within 14 days).

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
